evidence: fetcher.py:259 `_iter_pages(client, jql, ...)` calls `client.search_issues(jql, start_at=start_at, max_results=page_size)` — offset protocol

The plan names one precedent (_iter_pages, offset) for a token protocol it also declares distinct ('token=Cloud-v3')
findings.finding: The plan reuses fetcher._iter_pages as the precedent/host for migrating acli_graph.py's token loops, but _iter_pages is an OFFSET (startAt) pager while the acli_graph loops are opaque-nextPageToken cursor loops whose own docstrings record startAt is HTTP-400-rejected on /rest/api/3/search/jql; the token iterator is therefore new behavior (CREATION) the plan does not specify.
findings.location: Approach (2): 'One paged-iterator per pagination PROTOCOL (offset=DC, token=Cloud-v3) following fetcher._iter_pages'
scenarios: Implementer tries to route the three Cloud token loops through _iter_pages and breaks them because search_issues offset semantics don't apply to the /search/jql cursor endpoint
The 'token' iterator is silently a new component with no specified termination contract (isLast vs null token vs same-token-twice)
findings.suggested_fix: Split Approach (2) into two named iterators: an offset iterator (the existing _iter_pages, startAt-driven, DC) and a new cursor iterator (nextPageToken/isLast, Cloud-v3 /search/jql) that the three acli_graph maps consume; drop 'following fetcher._iter_pages' for the token case.

test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py docstring: 'Cloud's readers page CORRECTLY today — they are cursor-driven (echo the server's opaque token back) rather than offset-driven, so the advance-by-requested-size arithmetic that broke DC does not exist here.'
findings.finding: The plan says migrate acli_graph.py's token (nextPageToken/Cloud-v3) loops onto an iterator 'following fetcher._iter_pages', but _iter_pages implements the OFFSET protocol (drives client.search_issues(start_at=, max_results=), advances start_at += len(page)); it does not speak the nextPageToken cursor the acli_graph readers use. The two are structurally different protocols, so the named migration target cannot host the token loops as written.

findings.suggested_fix: Specify two iterators: keep/extend the offset `_iter_pages` for `search_issues` callers, and add a NEW token/cursor iterator for the `/search/jql` nextPageToken readers; state the token pager only parallels `_iter_pages` in shape, not code path.

The 9263 structural gate may flag the new/moved offset callers.

findings.finding: The plan does not address the known unfixed runaway-cursor failure mode of the token loops (a server repeating the same cursor spins the loop forever, strict-xfail/bug cabc), even though the offset pager it points at (_iter_pages) has explicit same-token-twice and offset-stall guards. A shared token iterator is exactly where that guard would live; leaving it unspecified risks reproducing the loop-forever hole in the consolidated iterator.
